source: Bossard et al. (2022) NDM in sport, Frontiers in Psychology
finding: The paper cites a review (Macquet 2020) with RPD level usage in sport experts. Most decisions are simple matches. It cites no AI or computational RPD model.
numbers: Simple match 60-81%; diagnosis 13-28%; evaluation by simulation 3-24%. Experts chose their first option in about 80% of decisions. No sample sizes given.
limits: Mostly qualitative interview work. Rates come second-hand from a review.
agent_relevance: A sport-trained agent should expect fast pattern match to cover most cases and simulation to be rare, so simulation should be gated, not default.

source: Bossard et al. (2022) - machine gap
finding: The paper lists sport RPD studies (football umpires, badminton, volleyball, handball goalkeepers, judo, rugby coaches). It mentions only 360-degree camera and VR as new methods. No LLM or ML test of RPD in sport is cited.
numbers: About 14 sport study groups named; 0 AI studies.
limits: Absence in one review is not proof none exists.
agent_relevance: Machine tests of RPD in sport are an open gap; our evidence is indirect (sport QA, tactics AI, real-time agents).

source: Xia et al. (2024) SportQA: sports understanding benchmark for LLMs
finding: LLMs know sport facts and rules but fail on expert scenario questions. GPT-4 is best but far below human experts on scenario items.
numbers: 70,592 multiple-choice items. Level-1 21,385, Level-2 45,685, Level-3 3,522. GPT-4 5-shot CoT: L1 85.63, L2 78.82, L3 easy single-hop 73.58, hard single-hop 64.08, easy multi-hop 34.40, hard multi-hop 23.01. Human experts (student-athletes): 96.63, 96.02, 94.90, 91.84 on the four L3 sets. Llama2-13b L3 hard multi-hop 5.86-9.20.
limits: Multiple-choice text only. Human L3 scores from athletes in each sport, small panel. Level-3 coverage limited per the authors.
agent_relevance: Gap grows with scenario difficulty and number of hops. The agent needs a multi-step situation-to-action check, not a bigger model alone.

source: Xia et al. (2024) SportQA: prompting effect
finding: Few-shot examples helped more than chain-of-thought on easy levels. CoT often did not help and sometimes hurt on hard scenario items.
numbers: GPT-4 L1: 0-shot CoT 80.60, 5-shot standard 80.24, 5-shot CoT 85.63. GPT-4 hard multi-hop: 22.59 (0S CoT), 24.69 (5S standard), 23.01 (5S CoT). PaLM2 hard single-hop: 5S standard 49.80 vs 5S CoT 38.37. GPT-3.5 L1: 5S standard 74.74 vs 0S CoT 49.04.
limits: Single run per setting; no variance reported.
agent_relevance: Worked examples (a recognition library) beat generic step-by-step thinking here, as RPD predicts.

source: Xia et al. (2024) SportQA: error analysis
finding: GPT-4 mistakes on level-3 are mostly concept errors, not logic errors. It cannot tie a concept to the scene.
numbers: 20 wrong answers per group analysed by hand. 82.5% of level-3 errors: inadequate multifaceted answer identification. Conceptual misunderstanding 55% (single-hop) and 50% (multi-hop) of errors. Levels 1-2: 40% conceptual deficiency.
limits: Small manual sample, GPT-4 only.
agent_relevance: The missing skill is cue recognition (which features of the scene matter), the first RPD step. Add an explicit cue-listing step.

source: Xia et al. (2025) SPORTU: multimodal sports understanding benchmark
finding: Text LLMs and video models stay well below experts on rule application and foul detection. GPT-4o best on text.
numbers: SPORTU-text 900 items; video 1,701 clips, 12,048 QA pairs, 7 sports. GPT-4o 71% best text (5-shot CoT). Claude-3.5-Sonnet 64.33 (0S), 68.44 (5S). Video: Qwen2-VL-72B 70.94% overall but 44.12% on hard; Claude-3.5-Sonnet 52.57% on hard, 70.18% overall.
limits: Multiple-choice; built from broadcast clips, not live play.
agent_relevance: Hard perceptual judgment stays weak even for the best model; do not trust the agent on novel, fast scene reads.

source: Xia et al. (2025) SPORTU: reasoning first hurts
finding: Asking the video model to write reasoning first lowered accuracy compared with answering directly.
numbers: Claude-3.5-Sonnet hard video task: 52.57% direct vs 39.32% rationale first (13.25 point drop). Order across models: direct answer > answer then rationale > rationale first.
limits: Video side only; text-side CoT effects were mixed.
agent_relevance: Matches the NDM claim that verbalising before recognising can disrupt expert pattern match. Answer first, justify second, then check.

source: Xia et al. (2025) SPORTU: camera-angle consistency
finding: The same play from several camera angles gets inconsistent answers, so models do not hold a stable situation model.
numbers: P(all angles correct)/P(all wrong)/mixed: Claude-3.5-Sonnet 52.86/18.59/28.55; GPT-4o 47.42/20.84/31.73; Gemini 1.5 Pro 43.24/25.41/31.35; GPT-4o-mini 36.89/28.40/34.72; Video-ChatGPT 25.06/35.84/39.10.
limits: 28-39% of questions got mixed results even for strong models.
agent_relevance: A cheap self-check: ask the same situation in several framings and flag disagreement as low confidence.

source: Yang et al. (2024) Sports Intelligence: LLM and video-LM sports benchmark
finding: Six months after SportQA, basic knowledge rose a little while scenario analysis rose more. GPT-4 and GPT-4o lead.
numbers: Level-1: GPT-4 83.70-84.05, GPT-4o 72.85-85.35, Gemini 1.5 Pro up to 79.15. Hard multi-hop scenario: GPT-4 22.78-31.65, GPT-4o 22.78-29.11, Claude 3 Opus 26.16-29.11. Paper reports gains over SportQA of roughly 4.5%, 7.0%, 10% and 7% on the four scenario subsets.
limits: Best of several iterations reported; small subsets; same Level-3 data as SportQA so contamination is possible.
agent_relevance: Scenario gains arrive fast; re-test periodically rather than assume the gap is fixed.

source: Yang et al. (2024) Sports Intelligence: CoT inconsistent
finding: Chain-of-thought effect was mixed across models. It helped GPT-4o on Level-1 but lowered some Claude and Gemini scores.
numbers: GPT-4o L1: 81.70 (0S) vs 85.35 (0S CoT). Claude 3 Opus L1: 66.67 (0S) vs 58.73 (0S CoT). Gemini 1.5 Pro L1: 75.90 (0S CoT) vs 67.45 (5S CoT). Authors still conclude CoT helps on complex reasoning.
limits: No repeated runs or intervals.
agent_relevance: Make reasoning mode a tunable switch per task, not a fixed rule.

source: Hu et al. (2024) SportsMetrics: information fusion in LLMs
finding: Given play-by-play text from NBA and NFL games, LLMs cannot reliably track state (score, yards), more so as games get longer.
numbers: GPT-4-1106-preview: 34.77-yard discrepancy in NFL passing yards. In one task 79% of one model JSON outputs held zeros or nulls. GPT-3.5-Turbo-1106 and Gemini-Pro stayed flat with game length; GPT-4 degraded on long games.
limits: Tests numeric tracking, not tactical choice. Late-2023 model versions.
agent_relevance: Recognition needs an accurate situation state. Give the agent a ledger or tool for state rather than trusting memory of long streams.

source: Wang et al. (2024) TacticAI: an AI assistant for football tactics (DeepMind and Liverpool FC)
finding: Geometric deep learning on corner kicks predicts receiver and shot and suggests player moves. Experts could not tell its suggestions from real ones and preferred them to existing tactics most of the time.
numbers: Receiver top-3 accuracy 0.782 +/- 0.039; shot F1 0.64 +/- 0.02. Five Liverpool raters, 50 corners: real-vs-generated F1 0.60 +/- 0.04. Raters top-3 accuracy 0.79 +/- 0.18 (real 0.82, generated 0.77). Abstract: favoured over existing tactics 90% of the time.
limits: Five raters (three data scientists, one video analyst, one coaching assistant); no match-outcome trial; data not public; not an LLM.
agent_relevance: A retrieve-similar-case-then-adjust tool fits expert pattern libraries for set pieces. Supports that loop for our agent.

source: Wang et al. (2024) TacticAI: similar-case retrieval
finding: TacticAI embeddings retrieve similar past corners, rated useful by coaches. Raters agreed on retrieval and refinement quality.
numbers: Retrieval ratings did not differ across raters (F(1,4)=1.01, p>0.1); refinement ratings agreed (F(1,4)=0.45, p>0.05). Rater C rated realism differently from the others.
limits: Five people; non-significance is weak evidence of agreement.
agent_relevance: Case retrieval is the machine form of RPD pattern match; judge it by expert ratings, not only accuracy.

source: Kurach et al. (2020) Google Research Football: an RL environment
finding: Open football simulator for agents. Baselines (IMPALA, PPO, Ape-X DQN) handle easy scenarios and struggle with full games and the Corner scenario.
numbers: Three full-game levels (easy, medium, hard) and 11 Football Academy scenarios. Corner is the hardest academy scenario. Multi-agent test on 3 vs 1 with Keeper, 1 to 3 controlled players.
limits: RL from scratch, no language, no recognition-primed structure.
agent_relevance: A simulator where an LLM or RPD agent could be compared with trained RL baselines.

source: Ma et al. (2024) Large Language Models Play StarCraft II (TextStarCraft II, Chain of Summarization)
finding: LLM agents act in a real-time game through text. A summarising loop (Chain of Summarization) lets most beat the built-in AI.
numbers: Ten LLMs tested; most beat the Level-5 built-in AI. Wins out of 20: Gemini-Pro 11, GLM4 12, Claude 2.1 5. Llama2 70B could not follow the command format.
limits: Text interface to a game, not human sport; scripted opponent.
agent_relevance: Real-time sport-like decisions need compact state summaries. Chain of Summarization is an agent-loop method that fits.

source: Ma et al. (2024) TextStarCraft II: prompt structure effect
finding: A prompt forcing phases (situation overview, analysis, plan, decision) beat a simple prompt by a large margin, mostly at harder levels.
numbers: GPT-3.5-turbo-16k win rate, Prompt 1 vs Prompt 2: LV3 25% vs 100%; LV4 12.5% vs 84%; LV5 0% vs 50%; LV6 0% vs 8.33%.
limits: One model, one race matchup (Protoss vs Zerg); small game counts per cell.
agent_relevance: A staged prompt mirroring RPD (read situation, assess, plan, act) lifted real-time results. Supports a stage-based scaffold.

source: Ma et al. (2024) TextStarCraft II: fine-tuning data and humans
finding: Fine-tuning on only the best wins beat fine-tuning on all games. A small fine-tuned model matched a Gold-level human but lost to stronger players.
numbers: Fine-tune on wins from top 25% by APU: 54/100 wins; full dataset: 28/100. Human matches (10 each): Pro 0/10, Grandmaster 0/10, middle player 5/10, Gold player 10/10 (reported as LLM wins).
limits: CoT removed for fine-tuning; few human opponents.
agent_relevance: Expert-quality cases matter more than volume, the same point NDM makes about expert case libraries.

source: Liu et al. (2025) Mind Your Step (by Step): CoT can reduce performance where thinking makes humans worse (ICML)
finding: Tested whether tasks where verbal thought hurts humans also hurt models with chain-of-thought. In three of six task types, yes, including face recognition and implicit pattern learning, the tacit recognition NDM stresses.
numbers: Implicit statistical learning: o1-preview vs GPT-4o absolute drop 36.3%. Face recognition CoT drops: GPT-4o 23.1%, Claude 3 Opus 8.0%, Gemini 1.5 Pro 6.05%, Llama 3.1 70B 8.8%; Claude 3.5 Sonnet -1.8%. Learning with exceptions took up to 331% more trials.
limits: Not sport. Models and humans do not share all processes; three of six task types showed no consistent drop.
agent_relevance: Do not force long reasoning on pure recognition steps. Keep it for diagnosis and simulation steps.

source: Suri et al. (2023) Do LLMs show decision heuristics similar to humans? GPT-3.5 case study
finding: GPT-3.5 shows anchoring, conjunction fallacy, framing and endowment effects like humans. Heuristic bias, the opposite pole to NDM expert intuition, appears in models too.
numbers: Anchoring: low anchor mean 20.83, high 105.97 for ChatGPT (t(58)=8.78); humans 22.5 and 80.50 (t(58)=5.55). Conjunction choice: ChatGPT 18 of 20, humans 10 of 20.
limits: Small cells (about 20), one old model, online human sample, not about expertise.
agent_relevance: A recognition step can import biased cues. Pair it with a debias check (see Heuristics-and-biases subfield).

source: Fan, Sun, McNeese, Yen (2005) Extending the recognition-primed decision model to support human-agent collaboration
finding: Software agents built on an RPD architecture to support human teammates. Metadata only; abstract not retrievable.
numbers: 74 citations per Semantic Scholar (2026-11-17).
limits: Not opened; only title and metadata verified.
agent_relevance: Oldest agent form of RPD; a template for a language-model RPD loop.

source: Fan and Yen (2008) Team-RPD: a collaborative model of the recognition-primed decision process
finding: Extends RPD to teams of agents. Metadata only.
numbers: 1 citation per Semantic Scholar.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Team sports are team RPD; this is the computational version.

source: Nowroozi, Shiri, Aslanian, Lucas (2012) A general computational recognition primed decision model with multi-agent rescue simulation benchmark
finding: Computational RPD tested on a multi-agent rescue simulation benchmark. Metadata only; results unread.
numbers: 24 citations per Semantic Scholar.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: A benchmarked RPD agent exists, but outside sport and before LLMs.

source: Hu, Li, Zhang (2018) Predicting pilot behavior during midair encounters using recognition primed decision model
finding: RPD used as a predictor of pilot choices. Metadata only.
numbers: 13 citations per Semantic Scholar.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: RPD can serve as a predictor of expert action, not only a description.

source: Ivanova, Didenko, Grigoryan, Kraevskiy (2025) Simulating dynamics of the recognition-primed decision model on financial markets using LLM
finding: Book chapter simulating RPD with an LLM in finance. Only the title and authors were retrieved.
numbers: None retrieved.
limits: Not opened; possibly the closest direct LLM-RPD study. Needs full text.
agent_relevance: Check later for prompt design and measured results.

source: Susceptibility to misinformation: persuasion and prior orientation in recognition-primed decision pathways (J. Cognitive Engineering and Decision Making, 2026)
finding: Study of how misinformation steers RPD pathways. Publisher page returned 403; title only.
numbers: None retrieved.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: If false cues steer the match step, the agent needs a cue-source check.

source: Search coverage note 2026-11-17
finding: OpenAlex, arXiv API and Semantic Scholar search were rate limited and the WebSearch budget was spent; Crossref and direct arXiv PDFs worked. No LLM test of sport RPD itself was found.
numbers: 0 direct LLM-on-sport-RPD studies found.
limits: Absence reflects limited search, not proof.
agent_relevance: Treat direct LLM-RPD-in-sport as open; retry with a fresh quota.
